# `min-properties-increased`

minProperties increased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `min-properties-increased` (both directions), `min-properties-increased-in-request`, `min-properties-increased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`minProperties` increased.

## Why this default

In requests: objects with fewer properties are now rejected. In responses: clients receive objects with at least as many properties as before.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  min-properties-increased: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the old minimum in requests.
